edges.description: The fusion is taken to drive the tumour's expression of epithelial, mesenchymal and neural markers together. The link is indirect. The fusion is shown to control the gene expression programme that characterises primary tumours, and the first molecular study proposed that the partner gene of EWS accounts for the biological differences between the tumours that carry an EWS fusion. No study cited here shows which target genes produce the mixed marker expression.

Expression of the fusion protein induced the endogenous PDGFA gene in an inducible cell model, and wild-type WT1 did not regulate it. In tissue, PDGFA was expressed within the tumour cells of primary tumours and was absent in Wilms tumours expressing WT1 and in Ewing sarcomas with an EWS-FLI translocation.

PDGFA is a growth factor for fibroblasts, and the study that identified it as a target of the fusion concluded that it contributes to the reactive fibrosis around the nests of tumour cells. The conclusion rests on the expression of PDGFA in the tumour cells. The response of the stromal fibroblasts was not measured.

nodes.description: Nests of tumour cells are separated by an abundant fibrous stroma, the feature the tumour is named for. The first series of 19 cases listed an intense desmoplastic reaction among the main features of the entity, and a later study describes massive reactive fibrosis surrounding the nests of tumour cells.

evidence.snippet: Diagnosis is based on histological analysis of biopsies which typically show small round blue cells in nests separated by an abundant desmoplastic stroma.

nodes.description: The t(11;22)(p13;q12) translocation fuses EWSR1 on chromosome 22 with WT1 on chromosome 11. The resulting fusion protein contains the potent transcriptional activation domain of EWSR1 fused to the zinc finger DNA-binding domain of WT1. This chimeric transcription factor activates aberrant gene expression programs including PDGFA. The chimeric transcripts join the amino-terminal domain of EWS in frame to the last three zinc fingers of WT1, in both alternatively spliced forms. Silencing the fusion in two tumour cell lines showed that they depend on it, and the two isoforms of the fusion, which differ in the DNA-binding domain, were both needed to generate xenograft tumours that resemble primary disease.

nodes.description: DSRCT displays a unique multiphenotypic immunophenotype with co-expression of epithelial (cytokeratin, EMA), mesenchymal (vimentin, desmin), and neural (NSE) markers. This reflects the aberrant differentiation program driven by EWSR1-WT1.

nodes.description: EWSR1-WT1 directly activates transcription of PDGFA, creating an autocrine growth loop that stimulates tumor cell proliferation and may contribute to the characteristic desmoplastic stromal reaction.

evidence.reference_title: The EWS-WT1 translocation product induces PDGFA in desmoplastic small round-cell tumour.
evidence.snippet: Expression of EWS-WT1 induced the expression of endogenous platelet-derived growth factor-A (PDGFA), a potent secreted mitogen and chemoattractant whose promoter contains the many potential WT1-binding sites.

evidence.reference_title: The EWS-WT1 translocation product induces PDGFA in desmoplastic small round-cell tumour.
evidence.snippet: the oncogenic fusion of EWS to WT1 in DSRT results in the induction of PDGFA, a potent fibroblast growth factor that contributes to the characteristic reactive fibrosis associated with this unique tumour.
